header: Date: 2026-09-29 | Start: 16:00 PDT | Duration: 52m | Redwood: Aaron Patel, Sam Wu, Priya Nair | Kestrel: Lena Ortiz (CTO), Mika Tan (ML Eng), Jordan Price (DevOps), Rajiv (Prod)
summary: Intro + catalog walkthrough focusing on model selection for low-latency checkout queries, benching approach, routing/fallbacks, and security requirements. Customer wants 200ms p50/p95 targets for short sequences and clear costs. Agreed to a pilot benchmark and to exchange security docs and sample prompts.
topics: Catalog UI demo, compatibility matrix filters, benchmark interpretation, kernel mapping / quant profiles, routing policies (latency vs cost), private vs hosted tradeoffs, SOC2/KMS/audit logs, pilot next steps
transcript:
[00:00] Aaron (AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, quick check who we have; I see Lena, Mika, Jordan and Rajiv from Kestrel; hi from Redwood it's Aaron and Sam and Priya.
[00:10] Lena (CTO): Hi thanks, excited to see how your catalog maps to our checkout latency constraints.
[00:18] Aaron: Great, goal for today is to walk through the model catalog in Console, show bench signals and compatibility matrix, and how Optimize suggests batching/quantization settings. We'll leave time for security questions.
[00:30] Sam (SE): I'll drive the Console live demo -- starting from the catalog landing, you can filter by task, cost per 1k tokens, expected latency on H100/A100, and quantization support.
[00:45] Sam: One thing to call out, our latency numbers are from internal benches with typical e-commerce sequences; they vary with context length and KV cache hit rates.
[00:58] Mika (ML Eng): When you say latency per model, is that cold start or steady-state? We care mostly about tail for 8-token responses.
[01:08] Sam: Good question — the profile shows steady-state p50/p95 for 8-16 token responses on the target GPU family. There's an extra cold-start row for initial session creation.
[01:20] Priya: Also note Optimize will recommend kernel/quant profiles for your workload distribution; if most requests are short it may suggest int8 quant for specific architectures to hit cost targets.
[01:33] Jordan (DevOps): Our constraint is a 200ms p95 for checkout microcopy generation; if the hosted API can't guarantee that we need private deployment.
[01:44] Aaron: Understood. We have routing policies so you can route high-priority traffic to Dedicated pools with latency SLOs while sending background tasks to cost-optimized variants.
[01:55] Lena: Can you show that in the compatibility matrix?
[02:00] Sam: Sure -- switching to model "Compare" view. Here you can pin your target hardware (H100) and set a latency budget filter at 200ms. The matrix highlights models that meet the budget at the configured batch size.
[02:20] Sam: See these flags — quantization friendly, kernel mapped, recommended variant. You can also toggle sequence length and batching policy to see how win/loss changes.
[02:35] Rajiv (Product): How do you compute cost estimates in the UI? Is that per-token or per-inference?
[02:42] Sam: Per-token base but we show effective cost per-request based on average tokens and batching. Optimize simulates batching gains using your histograms if you upload them.
[02:55] Mika: If we do int8, any quality regressions? How do we measure?
[03:02] Priya: We hook into your eval sets — you can upload a prompt set and Redwood will run comparative evals across quant/variants and show metric deltas (exact-match, BLEU-ish metrics, or custom business metrics).
[03:18] Lena: We need to see real QA on our checkout prompts — bootstrapping a sample set should be straightforward.
[03:26] Aaron: Perfect, action item for Kestrel to share 10-20 representative prompts after the call. We'll run bench + quality comparisons.
[03:35] Jordan: On networking, what's required for Dedicated vs Private? We run in AWS with strict egress rules.
[03:42] Sam: Dedicated supports VPC peering and private link; Private (Private Control Plane) can be deployed into your VPC/on-prem for fully customer-managed networking. Both integrate with KMS for key management.
[03:56] Jordan: And audit logs? We need immutable logs for compliance.
[04:01] Aaron: Yes — audit trails and request/response metadata retention are available, and our enterprise package includes extended retention and SIEM hooks.
[04:11] Lena: SOC 2 and ISO?
[04:13] Priya: We have SOC2 Type II reports and ISO attestations, plus a security whitepaper. I'll share those after the call.
[04:22] Rajiv: Back on model selection, suppose a model meets latency but is more expensive token-wise; can you do routing by cost tier?
[04:30] Sam: Yes — you can create policy rules: e.g., route 95% of traffic to cost-optimized variant and 5% to low-latency Dedicated variant, or route by user segments. There is a canary rollout mechanism for gradual migration.
[04:44] Mika: For our bench, we'd like to see kernel mapping: which layers are falling back to slower kernels and whether quantization gains are realized on our H100s.
[04:53] Sam: We attach a kernel compatibility report to bench runs. It shows unsupported ops and estimated fallback costs; also kernel-level recommendations for compilation flags.
[05:05] Aaron: For this pilot we recommend running three short tests: 1) throughput/latency on hosted with representative requests, 2) same on Dedicated with pinned GPUs, 3) quality comparison across float16 vs int8. Sam will own the bench plan.
[05:20] Sam: I'll send a bench plan template; it includes sequences per user, expected p50/p95 targets, and suggested batch sizes.
[05:28] Jordan: How do you preserve PII in the request logs — can we mask or avoid storing payloads?
[05:35] Priya: We can mask request bodies, redact tokens, and route logs to your S3 with server-side encryption. For Private deployments the customer retains full control of logs.
[05:48] Lena: What about data residency — can we keep data in EU regions only?
[05:52] Aaron: Yes, region targeting is supported and Dedicated pools can be pinned to region; Private deployment gives full data residency control.
[06:00] Rajiv: Any known regressions when using continuous batching with KV cache enabled? We saw some coherence issues elsewhere.
[06:08] Sam: Continuous batching should not affect output determinism for identical inputs; KV cache changes only if session-level caching is enabled and you reuse contexts. We'll show cache hit-rate charts in the bench report.
[06:22] Mika: One more on cost: do you have explicit per-model quantized pricing or is it simulated?
[06:29] Aaron: Simulated during bench estimates; billed per-token ultimately, but we provide model-specific per-token effective estimates to help budgeting. For Dedicated we offer committed capacity pricing options.
[06:40] Lena: Ok, let's talk schedule — timeline for a pilot? We are aiming to decide by mid-Oct.
[06:47] Aaron: We can have a 2-week pilot starting as early as Oct 6 if Kestrel provides prompts and we provision a sandbox. That should give enough data for p95/p50 and quality deltas.
[06:58] Jordan: Sandbox network access — what's the minimal footprint?
[07:02] Sam: API keys + IP allowlist or a VPC peering setup for secure access. We'll provide temporary keys scoped to the sandbox.
[07:12] Rajiv: Any gotchas integrating with our feature flagging system for canary routing?
[07:17] Priya: We have webhook hooks and a routing API that integrates with your feature flags; customers wire their internal flag to Redwood routing rules.
[07:26] Lena: Good. Can you also include a runbook for failover? We need clear behavior when a Dedicated pool is saturated.
[07:33] Aaron: Yes — Redwood supports automatic fallback to compatible model variants and region-level routing. We'll share sample runbooks.
[07:42] Mika: For the bench, please include kernel-level flamegraphs if possible; that helps our compilers team.
[07:46] Sam: We can include per-layer latency breakdowns and a kernel fallback summary.
[07:53] Aaron: Quick recap: Redwood sends pricing and SLA matrix, security docs, bench plan; Kestrel shares prompts, SLOs, and network constraints; set pilot start target Oct 6.
[08:05] Lena: Sounds good. One question I forgot — do you support model pinning per-route in the API?
[08:12] Sam: Yes, per-route model/version pinning plus rollout policies (canary/A-B/percent rollouts).
[08:18] Jordan: And how do we monitor token-level cost in real-time?
[08:22] Priya: The Console has token breakdowns per-route and cost estimation; we expose metrics to Prometheus and have export to billing reports.
[08:33] Rajiv: Great. Anything else?
[08:36] Aaron: That's it from our side. We'll follow up with the items discussed. Thanks everyone.
[08:42] Lena: Thanks all.
[08:44] (call ends)
